surprising_connections.insight: Oracle reasoning strategies auto-select based on CWE type, similar to how genome features map to attack patterns
surprising_connections.why: Both systems use pattern matching + heuristics, but Oracle is deterministic while Genome is ML-based

surprising_connections.insight: Both avoid expensive operations (RAG avoids embeddings, Council avoids model swaps via batching)
surprising_connections.why: Shared optimization philosophy: minimize VRAM/latency without sacrificing quality

surprising_connections.insight: Red Team mutations use same obfuscation techniques as XSS payloads
surprising_connections.why: Both need to evade detection (WAF for immune, CSP for XSS)

surprising_connections.insight: ScanContext is thread-safe despite async execution because each scan gets its own instance
surprising_connections.why: Async coordination without explicit locking - each scan_id maps to isolated context

surprising_connections.insight: Both capture multi-perspective reasoning but Tree is single-model sequential, Debate is multi-model parallel
surprising_connections.why: Different approaches to exploring solution space with audit trails

surprising_connections.insight: Patch agent could theoretically use terminal to verify patches by running tests, but currently relies on verification gate
surprising_connections.why: Missed integration opportunity - terminal is only used by attack agents, not remediation

suggested_questions: How does Oracle's automatic strategy selection prevent small 7B models from generating shallow patches?
What makes the vectorless RAG approach faster than embedding-based retrieval for code context?
How does the adversarial co-evolution converge without overfitting to specific attack patterns?
Why does the council use Agent-Centric Batching instead of loading all models simultaneously?
How does ScanContext flow through parallel attack agents without race conditions?
What's the relationship between CWE types and Oracle reasoning strategies?
How does the behavioral genome combine ML scores with heuristic scores for better accuracy?
Why is the CVS terminal implemented in pure Python instead of using subprocess?
How does the patch verification gate prevent bad fixes without requiring human review?
What role does the knowledge tree play in grounding LLM patch generation?

offline_first_design.description: 100% local execution with zero cloud dependencies
offline_first_design.benefit: Works in air-gapped environments, no data exfiltration risk

multi_paradigm_security.description: Combines 5 distinct security approaches in one pipeline
multi_paradigm_security.benefit: Each paradigm catches vulnerabilities the others miss

agent_centric_batching.description: Load model once, process all tasks, unload
agent_centric_batching.optimization: Reduces model swaps from O(N×M) to O(M)
agent_centric_batching.benefit: 10x faster council execution on limited VRAM

vectorless_rag.approach: Multi-signal scoring: route match + CWE relevance + payload terms
vectorless_rag.benefit: 0 VRAM overhead, <50ms queries, no vector DB needed

adversarial_evolution.description: Red Team vs Blue Team genetic algorithm
adversarial_evolution.mechanism: Red mutates blocked payloads, Blue retrains on bypassed payloads
adversarial_evolution.convergence: Stops at 99%+ block rate or exhaustion
adversarial_evolution.benefit: Genome adapts to specific application behavior

oracle_reasoning.selection: Auto-selected by CWE type, severity, and task
oracle_reasoning.example: CMDi (CWE-78) always gets Tree-of-Thoughts, Critical vulns get Self-Consistency
oracle_reasoning.benefit: 7B models perform like 70B models through structured reasoning

council_consensus.process: Each model independently reviews findings, majority vote required
council_consensus.anti_hallucination: No single model can hallucinate a vulnerability

verification_gate.rejection: Rejects patches with nosemgrep, eslint-disable, etc.
verification_gate.benefit: Bad patches never reach production code

cvs_terminal.description: Pure-Python virtual Linux terminal for agents
cvs_terminal.isolation: No actual subprocess spawning, simulated execution
cvs_terminal.benefit: Safe attack simulation without system access

scan_pipeline.context_propagation: ScanContext passed through all stages, accumulating data

council_flow.debate_protocol: Vuln → Model A vote → Model B vote → Model C vote → Majority consensus
council_flow.patch_review: Patch → Generator LLM → Reviewer 1 → Reviewer 2 → Reflexion loop if rejected

immune_evolution.generation_loop: Red generates → Blue scores → Blocked → Red mutates → Blue retrains → Repeat
immune_evolution.convergence: Stops when block_rate >= 0.99 or max_generations reached
immune_evolution.genome_persistence: Saved to disk, reloaded for future scans

frontend.ui: Dashboard with agent progress, vulnerability findings, terminal output

security_philosophy.core_principle: Security tools should not be a security risk
security_philosophy.offline_first: 100% local execution, zero cloud APIs, no data exfiltration
security_philosophy.no_api_keys: Runs entirely on Ollama, no OpenAI/Anthropic billing
security_philosophy.multi_model_consensus: No single AI can apply a patch (majority vote required)
security_philosophy.audit_trails: Full reasoning traces and terminal logs
